newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds rise on mild wholesale price data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds rise on mild wholesale price data.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks and bonds rose Thursday as a mild August wholesale price report eased inflation fears, but gains were limited as Wall Street braced for Friday's retail price data.
The dollar inched up to an eight-week high against the German mark, but eased against the Japanese yen.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 17.02 points at 5,771.94 after rising as high as 5,794.13 -- above its record close of 5,778.00 set on May 22.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,464 to 860 on heavy volume of 398 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"Core producer prices were down a little bit and jobless claims were up. Now people are more sanguine about the Federal Open Market Committee meeting," said Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

Wall Street has been betting that the Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee, which meets on Sept. 24, would raise interest rates modestly to cool inflation pressures but now, investors are having second thoughts.
"Some are thinking the Fed won't do anything and the stock market is moving ahead," Zagorski said.
The Labour Department reported that wholesale prices rose moderately last month, providing new evidence that inflation remains under control despite strong economic growth.

The Producer Price Index edged up 0.3 percent last month, after showing no change in July. The more closely-watched "core" PPI, which factors out volatile food and energy costs, actually fell 0.1 percent after rising 0.1 percent in July.

In a separate report, the government said new applications for unemployment benefits rose by 21,000 last week, with new filings jumping to 338,000, further calming fears that the economy was nearing so-called full employment, which could fuel wage inflation.
"The PPI made the market happy, and tomorrow's Consumer Price Index is seen relatively stable," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
On Friday, the government will release the Consumer Price Index for August.
In the inflation-sensitive bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was up 14/32, reducing its yield to 7.08 percent from Wednesday's close of 7.11 percent.
Late Thursday, the dollar fetched 1.5130 marks, up from 1.5110 late Wednesday, but slipped to 110.13 yen from 110.35.
Corn and soybean prices rose after a private weather forecaster predicted a 60 percent to 70 percent chance for a crop-killing frost before Midwest crops matured.
At the Chicago Board of Trade, December corn futures closed up 3-1/4 cents at $3.30 per bushel, and November soybeans closed up 9-1/2 cents at $8.14-1/2.
Oil markets betting on a new U.S. military assault against Iraq drove prices higher, ending a day fraught with tension and unease on what lies ahead for the world's preeminent oil producing region.
October oil futures contracts on the New York Mercantile Exchange ended 25 cents per barrel higher at $25 after rising as high as $25.30.

At the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, October live cattle futures set a contract high for the third consecutive day in reaction to meat packers raising bids for cattle. CME October set a new high of 73.200 cents per pound before closing at 73.175 cents, up 0.450 cent on the day.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index closed 27.0 points higher at 3,932.6, surpassing its previous peak of 3,918.7 set Aug. 28. In Tokyo, the key 225-share Nikkei average closed off 127.11 points at 20,443.93.
